backlog.spec: In featurize, replace GetFingerprintAsNumPy with the count variant (gen.GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) so each bit holds how many times an environment occurs instead of 0/1. Keep radius 2 and 2048 bits. Everything else (RandomForest settings, seed handling) stays the same.
backlog.title: Count-based Morgan fingerprints

backlog.spec: Set RADIUS = 3 and use count fingerprints (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy) with fpSize 4096 to reduce bit collisions at the larger radius. Keep the RandomForest unchanged otherwise.
backlog.title: Radius-3 count Morgan fingerprint

backlog.spec: Build the Morgan generator with an atom invariant generator based on feature invariants (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()), giving pharmacophore-like functional-class environments. Use count fingerprints, radius 2, 2048 bits.
backlog.title: Feature-Morgan (FCFP-style) invariant fingerprint

backlog.spec: In addition to the Morgan bits, compute all RDKit descriptors from Descriptors.descList for each molecule (replace NaN and inf with 0, clip to a large finite range). Concatenate them with the fingerprint matrix before fitting. Descriptors such as logP, TPSA and MW are known drivers of hepatic clearance.
backlog.title: Append RDKit 2D physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: Compute the 167-bit MACCS keys with rdMACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys for each molecule and concatenate them to the Morgan features before the RandomForest. This adds a compact set of curated substructure flags alongside the hashed fingerprint.
backlog.title: Add MACCS keys

backlog.spec: Compute atom-pair count fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, 1024 bits) and topological torsion counts (GetTopologicalTorsionGenerator, 1024 bits) per molecule. Concatenate them with the Morgan count fingerprint and fit the same RandomForest.
backlog.title: Add atom-pair and topological-torsion count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Before fitting, replace train_y with its rank transform (scipy.stats.rankdata divided by n, mapped to (0,1]). Fit the RandomForest on the ranks and return its predictions directly. Since the score is Spearman correlation, fitting on ranks removes the influence of extreme clearance values on the splits.
backlog.title: Rank-transform the target

backlog.spec: If all train_y values are non-negative, fit the model on log1p(train_y) and return expm1 of the predictions (or just the raw log-scale predictions, which give the same Spearman ranking). Otherwise fit on the untransformed values. Clearance is a positive, right-skewed quantity, so the log scale usually makes tree splits more balanced.
backlog.title: Log-transform the target

backlog.spec: Clip train_y to its 2nd and 98th percentiles before fitting the RandomForest, leaving test predictions unchanged. This limits the effect of a few very high or very low measured clearance values on leaf averages.
backlog.title: Winsorize extreme targets

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForest with a LightGBM regressor on the same Morgan count features: about 600 trees, learning_rate 0.03, num_leaves 15, min_child_samples 10, subsample 0.8 with subsample_freq 1, colsample_bytree 0.3, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8. Gradient boosting often outperforms bagged trees on fingerprint regression.
backlog.title: Switch to LightGBM regressor

backlog.spec: Replace the RandomForest with an XGBoost regressor (hist tree method) on the Morgan count features: 500 estimators, max_depth 5, learning_rate 0.03, subsample 0.8, colsample_bytree 0.3, min_child_weight 3, random_state=seed, nthread=8.
backlog.title: Switch to XGBoost regressor

backlog.spec: Use CatBoostRegressor with about 800 iterations, depth 6, learning_rate 0.05, l2_leaf_reg 5, rsm 0.3 (feature subsampling), random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8 on the Morgan count features. CatBoost's ordered boosting tends to regularize well on small tabular datasets like this one.
backlog.title: CatBoost regressor on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Train a RandomForest and a LightGBM regressor on the same features. Convert each model's test predictions to ranks, then average the two rank vectors with equal weight and return the average. Averaging ranks avoids scale mismatch between the two models.
backlog.title: Rank-average ensemble of RF and GBM

backlog.spec: Compute binary Morgan fingerprints for train and test. Build the Tanimoto similarity matrix K(a,b) = sum(min(a,b))/sum(max(a,b)) for count vectors (or the bit-vector Jaccard version). Fit sklearn SVR with kernel='precomputed' (C about 5, epsilon 0.05) on the training kernel and predict with the test-to-train kernel. Tanimoto kernels are the standard similarity measure for molecular property prediction.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-kernel support vector regression

backlog.spec: Use the same Tanimoto similarity matrix on count Morgan fingerprints as a precomputed kernel. Fit sklearn KernelRidge(kernel='precomputed', alpha around 0.3) on the standardized training targets and predict using the test-to-train kernel matrix. This is a smooth, similarity-weighted alternative to the random forest.
backlog.title: Kernel ridge with Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Build RDKit 2D descriptors (Descriptors.descList, NaN and inf replaced by 0, clipped). Standardize the columns with StandardScaler fit on training data, then fit sklearn SVR with RBF kernel (C=3, gamma='scale', epsilon=0.1) on the scaled descriptors. Return its predictions for the test molecules.
backlog.title: Scaled RBF SVR on descriptors

backlog.spec: Use sklearn MLPRegressor with hidden layers (256, 64), alpha=1e-3 (L2), early_stopping=True with validation_fraction 0.1, max_iter 500, learning_rate_init 1e-3, on standardized log-count Morgan features. Average the predictions of 5 networks with different random_state values derived from seed. Ensembling several small networks reduces variance.
backlog.title: Shallow MLP ensemble on fingerprints

backlog.spec: Swap RandomForestRegressor for ExtraTreesRegressor with the same N_TREES, max_features=0.3, min_samples_leaf=1, n_jobs=-1, random_state=seed. Extremely randomized split thresholds smooth the predictor and often help when the data are small and noisy.
backlog.title: Replace RandomForest with ExtraTrees

backlog.spec: Set MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF to 3 in the RandomForestRegressor. Leaves that average more molecules give smoother predictions and reduce overfitting to individual noisy measurements in a dataset of under a thousand molecules.
backlog.title: Larger minimum leaf size in RandomForest

backlog.spec: Change MAX_FEATURES from 0.3 to 'sqrt' in the RandomForestRegressor, which for 2048 bits means about 45 candidate features per split. Keep the other settings the same. This is a lower-bias, more-decorrelated setting than the current 0.3 fraction.
backlog.title: Tune max_features for RandomForest

backlog.spec: Set RandomForest bootstrap=True with max_samples=0.7 so each tree sees 70% of the training molecules. Subsampling without replacement decorrelates trees further and adds regularization on the small training set.
backlog.title: Bootstrap subsampling of training molecules

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, train three RandomForest models with seeds derived from the seed argument (seed, seed+1, seed+2), each with 300 trees, and average their predictions. Trees are the same family, so this only reduces random-forest variance beyond what one forest with 300 trees achieves.
backlog.title: Average several RandomForest seeds internally

backlog.spec: In featurize, parse each SMILES, keep only the largest covalently bonded fragment using rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser (or split on '.' and keep the largest piece by heavy-atom count), neutralize charges with rdMolStandardize.Uncharger, and then compute the fingerprint. Salts and counter-ions would otherwise dilute the fingerprint and mislead the model.
backlog.title: Canonicalize and strip salts before featurizing

backlog.spec: Compute a small set of interpretable features per molecule: Crippen logP (Descriptors.MolLogP), TPSA, number of H-bond donors and acceptors, rotatable bonds, aromatic ring count, and formal charge. Concatenate these 8 values to the Morgan fingerprint features, which lets trees use the strong lipophilicity signal directly.
backlog.title: Add Crippen logP, TPSA and HBD/HBA explicitly

backlog.spec: Compute the EState atom-level indices with rdkit.Chem.EState.Fingerprinter.FingerprintMol for each molecule, which returns count and sum vectors. Concatenate the two vectors with the Morgan count fingerprint and fit the RandomForest. EState indices encode electronic environment and polar character, which relate to metabolic stability.
backlog.title: Electrotopological state (EState) fingerprint features

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, fit a first RandomForest on the training features, keep only the top 300 features by feature_importances_, then refit a fresh RandomForest with the same settings on the reduced matrix and predict on the test features restricted to those columns. This removes noisy, rarely-used bits.
backlog.title: Feature selection by RF importance

backlog.spec: Before fitting, remove every feature column that is nonzero in fewer than 5 training molecules (compute on train_smiles only, apply the same mask to test). Rare bits mostly encode single-molecule noise, and removing them shrinks the feature matrix and speeds up the forest.
backlog.title: Drop constant and rare fingerprint bits

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training molecules into 5 inner folds (KFold shuffled with seed), get out-of-fold predictions for a RandomForest, a LightGBM model and a Ridge regression on standardized features, then fit a non-negative linear blend (scipy.optimize.nnls) on those out-of-fold predictions. Refit all base models on the full training set and apply the blend to the test predictions.
backlog.title: Stacked ensemble with inner out-of-fold blending

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, run a small grid over MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF in {1, 3, 5} and MAX_FEATURES in {0.1, 0.3, 'sqrt'} using 3-fold inner CV on the training molecules scored by Spearman correlation. Refit the RandomForest with the best combination on all training data and predict. Keep the grid small so each fit stays well inside the 10-minute limit.
backlog.title: Inner-CV hyperparameter selection for the forest

backlog.spec: Use LightGBM with a learning-rate schedule: start at learning_rate 0.1 for the first 100 rounds, then decay by a factor of 0.5 every 200 rounds (lightgbm callback reset_parameter), up to 800 rounds total, with early stopping disabled. The decay lets the model make coarse fits first and refine later, which reduces overfitting on the small dataset.
backlog.title: Learning-rate decay for gradient boosting

backlog.spec: Replace the regressor with LightGBM trained under a pairwise ranking objective (objective='lambdarank' or 'rank_xendcg') on Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits, using GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Treat the whole training set as one query group, with integer relevance labels made by binning train_y into about 10 quantile buckets. The Spearman loss depends only on ordering, so this optimises ordering directly rather than squared error. Keep the seed in random_state and keep n_estimators around 300 with learning_rate 0.05, num_leaves 15, and min_child_samples 10. Return the raw scores for the test molecules as the predictions.
backlog.title: LambdaRank objective with LightGBM on Morgan counts

backlog.spec: Keep the RandomForest but do not predict with the mean of the trees. For each test molecule, collect the predictions of every individual tree (estimators_ list) and return the median (or a trimmed mean, dropping the top and bottom 10%). The median is robust to the heavy-tailed leaf estimates that the log transform leaves behind, and it can change the ranking of molecules in the middle of the distribution. Keep the log1p target transform and the existing fingerprint settings unchanged.
backlog.title: Median of per-tree forest predictions

backlog.spec: Train three RandomForest models on the same Morgan fingerprints, each on a different target transform: raw y, log1p y, and sqrt y (or a Box-Cox-like power transform with lambda 0.25 when all values are non-negative). Invert each model's predictions back to the original scale, convert each to ranks within the test set, and return the average of the three rank vectors. This combines models that differ in how they weigh large and small clearance values, which should reduce the variance that a single transform carries.
backlog.title: Ensemble over several target transforms

backlog.spec: After the usual RandomForest predictions, build a Tanimoto similarity matrix over all molecules, training and test together, using Morgan bit vectors. Keep only the k=10 nearest training neighbours of each test molecule, and build a symmetric weighted graph from those edges. Run a few steps of label propagation: start from the RF predictions for the test molecules and the true training targets, then repeatedly average each node with its weighted neighbours, clamping the training nodes to their true values. Return the propagated values for the test molecules. This is a bold change, but it uses the test molecules' neighbourhood structure at inference time, which the current model ignores.
backlog.title: Transductive label propagation over the test-train similarity graph

backlog.spec: Before fitting, denoise the training targets. For each training molecule, compute its Tanimoto similarity to the other training molecules on Morgan bit vectors, and take the k=5 nearest neighbours that are not in the same Murcko scaffold group. Replace the target with a convex combination: 0.7 times its own log1p value plus 0.3 times the similarity-weighted mean of the neighbours' log1p values. Fit the RandomForest on these shrunken targets, then predict in log space and invert. This regularises against label noise and assay variability while keeping the fingerprints unchanged. Use the seed for any tie-breaking.
backlog.title: Shrink noisy training targets toward their chemical neighbours

backlog.spec: Replace the standard bootstrap in the forest with scaffold-level bagging. Compute the Murcko scaffold of each training molecule, then build many small RandomForest models (for example 30 models of 20 trees each, or a manual ensemble of single DecisionTreeRegressor fits). Each sub-model is trained on a random 70% of the distinct scaffolds, with all molecules from a selected scaffold included together. Average the sub-model predictions. Because the test folds hold out whole scaffolds, this bagging matches the evaluation's grouping and may reduce scaffold-specific overfitting. Use the seed to draw the scaffold subsets.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped bagging of trees

backlog.spec: Compute a density weight for each training molecule: the reciprocal of the number of training molecules that share its Murcko scaffold, normalised so the weights average 1. Pass these weights as sample_weight to RandomForestRegressor.fit, so that large combinatorial scaffold families do not dominate the splits. Keep the log1p target transform and the Morgan features unchanged. Consider a softer variant with weight = count^-0.5 as a fallback if the first version looks unstable. This is a small change in what the forest learns from, and it targets the imbalance across skeletons.
backlog.title: Density-based reweighting of over-represented chemotypes

backlog.spec: Round one: fit the RandomForest on the training molecules with the log1p target, and predict the test molecules. Round two: add the test molecules to the training set with their round-one predictions as pseudo-labels, weighted at 0.3 relative to the true labels (use sample_weight). Refit the forest with a new seed and predict the test molecules again, and return these second-round predictions. This is a transductive self-training step. It is only valid because fit_predict receives all test SMILES at once, and it should be checked for overconfidence, since pseudo-labels can reinforce the model's own errors.
backlog.title: Two-round pseudo-labelling with the test molecules

backlog.spec: Train a LightGBM regressor on Morgan count fingerprints with the log1p target. Inside fit_predict, split the training molecules into an inner train and validation set by Murcko scaffold (about 80/20, using the seed). Train with early stopping on the inner validation Spearman or RMSE, using at most 2000 rounds at learning_rate 0.03, and record the best iteration. Refit on all the training molecules for 1.1 times the best iteration, then predict the test molecules. This sets the number of boosting rounds from the data instead of a fixed value, and the scaffold split keeps the inner validation honest.
backlog.title: Early stopping on an inner scaffold holdout for LightGBM rounds

backlog.spec: Compute the Tanimoto similarity between each test molecule and all training molecules on Morgan bit vectors. For each test molecule, take the k=7 most similar training molecules and average their log1p targets with weights equal to similarity raised to the power 3. Blend this kNN prediction with the RandomForest prediction (log space) using a fixed weight of 0.4 on kNN and 0.6 on the forest. Return the expm1 of the blended value. Neighbour averaging is a different inductive bias from tree splits on bits, so it may help when the test skeletons are far from the training set. Use the seed only for the forest.
backlog.title: Tanimoto-weighted kNN regression blended with the forest

backlog.spec: Keep the Tanimoto-kernel SVR, but choose C from {1, 3, 10, 30} and epsilon from {0.02, 0.05, 0.1} inside fit_predict. Split the training molecules into 4 inner folds grouped by Murcko scaffold, using the seed for the assignment. Score each (C, epsilon) pair by inner Spearman correlation on the log1p target, then refit on all training molecules with the best pair. Precompute the full training kernel once and slice it for the inner folds so the grid stays cheap.
backlog.title: Inner-CV grid search for SVR C and epsilon

backlog.spec: Replace the binary-style Tanimoto kernel with the MinMax kernel on the Morgan count vectors: K(a,b) = sum_i min(a_i,b_i) / sum_i max(a_i,b_i). Compute it by broadcasting min and max over the feature axis in chunks of about 100 rows so memory stays under 6 GB. Keep the log1p target, C=5 and epsilon=0.05 for the first run, then retune C only if the replicate is promising.
backlog.title: MinMax (weighted Jaccard) kernel on count fingerprints

backlog.spec: Build three count-Morgan fingerprints at radius 1, 2 and 3, plus a hashed atom-pair count fingerprint with 2048 bits. Compute a Tanimoto kernel for each and average them into one precomputed kernel, K = (K_r1 + K_r2 + K_r3 + K_ap)/4. Feed this combined kernel to the same SVR with precomputed kernel. Kernel averaging combines fingerprint families without concatenating them, so no single fingerprint dominates.
backlog.title: Multi-radius and atom-pair summed kernel

backlog.spec: For each test molecule, take its k=30 most Tanimoto-similar training molecules and fit a kernel ridge regression on that neighbourhood only, using the Tanimoto kernel restricted to those neighbours with a ridge penalty of 1.0. Predict the test value from the local model. Work in log1p space and undo it at the end. This is a locally weighted, non-global regressor that can adapt to each chemotype.
backlog.title: Local kernel ridge fitted per test molecule

backlog.spec: Optimise the rank order directly, since the score is Spearman. Sample about 40000 training pairs (i, j) with different targets, using the seed. For each pair, the feature is the difference of count-Morgan vectors x_i - x_j with label sign(y_i - y_j). Train a linear SVM (sklearn LinearSVC, C=0.5) on these difference vectors, with the pair labels as the classes. Score each test molecule by its dot product with the learned weight vector, which gives a ranking score. Use the test molecules' own feature vectors, not pairs.
backlog.title: Pairwise ranking SVM over sampled molecule pairs

backlog.spec: Fit the Tanimoto-kernel SVR on the log1p target. For the training set, get out-of-fold SVR predictions with a 5-fold inner split grouped by scaffold, and compute residuals = y - oof. Fit a small LightGBM (about 200 trees, learning rate 0.03, num_leaves 8) on RDKit descriptors (Crippen logP, TPSA, MolWt, HBD, HBA, rotatable bonds, aromatic ring count) to predict those residuals. Final prediction = SVR prediction + LightGBM residual prediction, computed on the test molecules.
backlog.title: Two-stage residual cascade: SVR then descriptor GBM

backlog.spec: Replace the epsilon-insensitive SVR with kernel ridge regression on the Tanimoto kernel, trained with Huber loss by iteratively reweighted least squares. Start with weights 1 and solve (K + lambda W^-1) alpha = y, with lambda = 1.0. After each solve, set the Huber weight for residual r to min(1, delta/|r|) with delta = 1.345 times the median absolute residual. Iterate 10 times and use the final alpha for prediction. This should stop the noisiest measurements from dominating the fit.
backlog.title: Huber-robust kernel regression by iteratively reweighted least squares

backlog.spec: For each molecule, compute the Murcko scaffold, the set of ring systems (fragments left after removing the linker atoms), and the generic scaffold with all atoms set to carbon. Hash each of these into a 512-bit count vector and append it to the Morgan count vector. Use the expanded vector for the Tanimoto kernel SVR. Scaffold-level identity is the axis that the grouped folds test on, so this gives the model a direct signal about how skeletons relate.
backlog.title: Ring-system and scaffold bag features added to the kernel

backlog.spec: Treat the Tanimoto kernel as a GP covariance: K_full = s^2 * K + sigma^2 * I. On the log1p target, pick s^2 and sigma^2 from a small log-grid (s^2 in {0.5, 1, 2}, sigma^2 in {0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4}) by maximising the GP log marginal likelihood computed with a Cholesky factor on the training kernel. Then predict the posterior mean for test molecules with alpha = K_full^-1 y. The GP setting is a principled way to pick the regularisation strength instead of fixing C and epsilon by hand.
backlog.title: Gaussian process regression on the Tanimoto kernel with learned noise

backlog.spec: Round 1: fit the Tanimoto SVR on the log1p target and get out-of-fold predictions for the training molecules using a 5-fold inner split grouped by scaffold. Round 2: build soft targets t = 0.7*y + 0.3*oof, then refit the same SVR on t and predict the test molecules. The blend pulls each label toward what the model thinks its chemical neighbours imply, which smooths label noise. Fix the blend weight at 0.3 and do not iterate further.
backlog.title: Self-distillation: second SVR round on blended soft targets

backlog.spec: Keep the existing Tanimoto-kernel SVR, but raise the kernel elementwise to a power p before fitting: K_train = K_train**p and K_test = K_test**p, with p = 2 (or choose p from {1, 2, 3} by an inner scaffold-grouped holdout on the training fold, using the seed for any split). Sharpening the kernel makes similarity more local, so distant molecules contribute less. Leave C and EPSILON unchanged. Output stays a predicted value per test molecule, and the log1p transform stays as it is.
backlog.title: Elementwise power of the Tanimoto kernel

backlog.spec: Build a composite kernel K = K_tanimoto * K_rbf, where K_rbf = exp(-gamma * ||d_i - d_j||^2) and d is a small standardized vector of 4 RDKit descriptors (Crippen MolLogP, TPSA, MolWt, number of aromatic rings). Standardize d using the training fold statistics only, and set gamma = 1 / number of descriptors. Use the product as a precomputed kernel for the same SVR with C=5 and EPSILON=0.05. This lets the model separate molecules that share substructures but differ in lipophilicity or polarity, which may matter for clearance. Keep the log1p target transform.
backlog.title: Product kernel: Tanimoto times RBF on physchem descriptors

backlog.spec: Train 15 SVR models, each on a random 60% subset of the Morgan count bits (chosen with a RandomState seeded from the seed argument, drawn without replacement). For each model, compute the Tanimoto kernel on its own bit subset only, so every model sees a different view of the chemistry. Average the 15 predictions for the test molecules (in the log1p space, then apply expm1). Each subset uses the same C and EPSILON. This is random-subspace ensembling, which is different from bootstrapping molecules.
backlog.title: Feature-subspace bagging of SVR

backlog.spec: Instead of one SVR with C=5, fit SVRs on the same Tanimoto kernel for C in {1, 5, 20}, with EPSILON scaled as 0.05 for each. Average their predictions in the log1p space before applying expm1. Averaging over the regularization strength hedges against the loss of the single chosen C. The kernel is computed once and reused for all three fits, so runtime stays small. No inner validation is needed.
backlog.title: Average SVR over a grid of C values

backlog.spec: Fit a first Tanimoto-kernel SVR (C=5, EPSILON=0.05) on the log1p target. Compute its in-sample predictions on the training molecules, and fit a second SVR with a smaller C (=1) on the residuals (y_log minus the first model's in-sample prediction). For test molecules, the final log-space prediction is the first model's prediction plus the second model's prediction. Convert back with expm1. Using a smaller C in the second round means the correction shrinks toward zero, which limits overfitting to noise.
backlog.title: Two-round residual kernel boosting

backlog.spec: Cluster the training molecules into K=4 groups with k-means (sklearn KMeans, n_init=5, random_state from seed) on their Morgan count vectors, after L2-normalizing each row. Fit a separate Tanimoto-kernel SVR (C=5, EPSILON=0.05) on each cluster's molecules. For each test molecule, find the nearest cluster centroid and predict with that cluster's SVR. If a cluster has fewer than 30 molecules, fall back to the global SVR fitted on all training molecules. Keep the log1p target transform. This is a hard gating mixture of local experts.
backlog.title: Cluster-routed mixture of SVR experts

backlog.spec: Before fitting the final SVR, compute leave-one-out predictions on the training molecules using the closed form for kernel-based models is not required: instead, run a 5-fold KFold on the training set (shuffled, random_state from seed) with the same Tanimoto SVR, collect out-of-fold predictions in log1p space, and drop the 5% of training molecules with the largest absolute out-of-fold residual. Refit the SVR (C=5, EPSILON=0.05) on the remaining molecules and predict the test set. Removing likely label-noise points is a form of robust regularization, distinct from shrinking targets.
backlog.title: Leave-one-out noise filtering before the final fit

backlog.spec: Use the test molecules (which are given to fit_predict) to weight the training data. For each training molecule i, compute w_i = max over test molecules j of the Tanimoto similarity between i and j, then clip to [0.1, 1] and normalize to mean 1. Pass these as sample_weight to SVR.fit (kernel precomputed, same C=5 and EPSILON=0.05). Training molecules that look like the test set get more influence, while molecules unrelated to the test chemistry are down-weighted. The test features are used only as unlabeled inputs.
backlog.title: Transductive test-similarity sample weighting

backlog.spec: Standardize the log1p target using the training-fold mean and standard deviation, fit the Tanimoto-kernel SVR on the standardized target, and set EPSILON = 0.1 * std of the standardized target (i.e. about 0.1 in z units) and C = 1 / (something tied to n) as C = 5 * sqrt(n_train / 800). Predict, undo the standardization, and apply expm1. This keeps the epsilon-tube and the penalty consistent when the target spread changes between CV folds, which is a plausible source of fold-to-fold variance.
backlog.title: Scale epsilon and C to the target spread

backlog.spec: Replace the Tanimoto kernel with a convex mixture K = 0.5 * K_tanimoto + 0.5 * K_cosine, where K_cosine is the cosine similarity of the Morgan count vectors (dot product divided by the product of L2 norms, with a small epsilon guard). Both are valid kernels, so their mixture is positive semidefinite and works with SVR(kernel='precomputed'). Keep C=5, EPSILON=0.05, and the log1p target. The cosine term rewards overall count-profile agreement, while the Tanimoto term rewards bit-level overlap.
backlog.title: Cosine and Tanimoto mixture kernel on count vectors

incumbent.description: Implement Tanimoto-kernel Support Vector Regression (SVR) as a similarity-based approach for predicting hepatocyte clearance.

memo: Helped: log1p target transform (slot 0, 0.5785, -0.0318 vs the 0.6103 baseline), count-based Morgan fingerprints (slot 11, 0.5676/0.5590, -0.0152), and above all Tanimoto-kernel SVR (slot 13, 0.5155, -0.0478; incumbent). Not helpful, within noise (sd about 0.0070): RF feature selection (+0.0027), CatBoost (+0.0028), winsorizing the target (+0.0000), rare-bit removal (+0.0013), and the slot 30 kernel variant (-0.0011, rejected). Worse than SVR: LightGBM (0.5400), XGBoost (0.5479), RF+LightGBM rank average (0.5534), KernelRidge (0.5254), radius 3 with 4096 bits (0.5244), MinMax kernel (0.5214). Many slots were wasted: 12 crashes (mostly RDKit API errors), 5 patch failures, and one broken run scoring 1.0000. Next: tune SVR C and epsilon, try a rank-transformed target, blend SVR with RF or CatBoost, and retry physchem descriptors using small, verified edits. Replicate any gain before accepting it.
